ai_summary: Great Britain is currently recording total GB wind output of 9.9 GW, underpinned by an estimated Scottish wind output of 4.0 GW, which represents 39.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Thanks to this abundant renewable volume, Scottish carbon intensity stands at 0 gCO2/kWh versus 129 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, severe transmission bottlenecks between Scotland and England prevent this surplus green electricity from flowing freely to southern demand centers. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 85.6 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £2,399,049. To replace this trapped zero-carbon generation, thermal power stations have fired up south of the border, leading to an estimated 16,258,604 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and emitting an additional 29,950 tonnes of CO2. Extrapolating today’s constraint expenditure yields an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £876 million. When these balancing expenses are recovered across national electricity demand, this grid friction increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £3/MWh, illustrating how transmission bottlenecks inflate system costs while directly compromising decarbonisation goals.
